figures.finding: Jamaica has no dedicated national film fund listed by its Film Commission: its financing page points to the CHASE Fund, which gives 15% of its grants and contributions to Arts and Culture and takes proposals for all or part funding of local film projects case by case (and backs the PROPELLA! script-to-screen programme with JAFTA and JAMPRO), and otherwise to development banks and foreign funds.

chaseFund.basis: case by case, all or part funding

figures.applies: Jamaica; as published by the Film Commission, read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: The CHASE Fund was originally enabled in 2002 from provisions from the betting and gaming industry but is now operated through The Consolidated Fund. The Fund currently allots 15 percent of its grants & contributions towards Arts & Culture and such applications may be made on an ongoing basis through its website for creative projects. CHASE has already shown its support of the developing local film industry through its partnership with JAFTA and JAMPRO on the PROPELLA! script to screen programme to encourage emerging filmmakers. On a case by case basis local producers, content creators, animators and filmmakers may also submit proposals for all or part funding of projects or the research and development of projects.

figures.finding: Jamaica's main film and television industry body is the Jamaica Film and Television Association (JAFTA), organised in 2015, whose members cross the industry; it runs PROPELLA! with the Film Commission and the CHASE Fund. No actors', writers' or directors' union or agreement is listed among the industry associations.

sources.said: The main industry association covering film and television is the Jamaica Film and Television Association (JAFTA). It’s members feature a cross-section of stakeholders in the industry who possess a wealth of skills and resources. JAFTA became an organised group in 2015. In collaboration with The Film Commission and The CHASE Fund, JAFTA has initiated PROPELLA!, an annual initiative aimed to encourage and support new filmmakers and expand the pool of creative producers working in the film and television industry.

figures.finding: Jamaica's investment agency JAMPRO runs the Jamaica Screen Development Initiative (JSDI, launched January 2024), which funds development, production, completion, festival and market attendance and production rebates: its first call drew 406 applications (269 validated, 90 selected), and its first rebate, the maximum US$1.5 million, went to Bob Marley: One Love for over US$20 million spent in Jamaica.

rebate.example: Bob Marley: One Love, over US$20m spent in Jamaica, approved by Cabinet 2023

figures.applies: Jamaica, as JAMPRO published on 18 February 2025 and the Gleaner reported on 23 October 2026; the rebate's rate and base were not found.

sources.said: The JSDI’s first call for applications in March 2024 resulted in 406 submissions, with 269 validated for further assessment. … For the 2024/25 Financial Year, JAMPRO received a budget allocation of J$234 million for JSDI. Of this amount, J$233,421,600.00 was disbursed for the first production rebate for Bob Marley: One Love , which was approved in 2023 by Cabinet to receive the maximum amount of US$1.5 million based on their over US$20m production expenditure in Jamaica.

90 film and screen projects have been selected for funding under the Government’s Jamaica Screen Development Initiative (JSDI), a $1-billion programme aimed at strengthening the country’s screen-based industries. The selected projects span five categories: development, production, completion, film festival and market attendance, and production rebates. The programme, administered by JAMPRO, received 406 applications following its 2024 call.
